paper.title: Non-Stationary Representation Learning in Sequential Linear Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Sequential linear bandits sharing a single representation (within-environment)
unmapped: Multi-task: a sequence of tau linear bandit tasks, each played for N rounds with known task boundaries; task parameter changes every N rounds
All task parameters lie in a common unknown r-dimensional subspace span(B) (shared representation); learner knows N and r but not tau
Task diversity assumption: every window of ell consecutive tasks has sigma_r(W W^T/ell) >= nu/r
Regret compared against per-round optimal action of the current task
settings.definition_quote: y_t= x_t^\top \theta_{q(t)} +\eta_t ... q(t)=\lceil t/N \rceil ... the action set $\CA$ is the ellipsoid of the form $\{x\in \R^d:x^\top M^{-1}x\le 1\}$ ... $\theta_{\min}\le \|\theta_s\| \le \theta_{\max}$

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-task sequential linear bandits in non-stationary environments (changing representations)
unmapped: S tasks played sequentially, N rounds each, from m environments in consecutive segments of unknown lengths tau_k
Each environment has its own unknown r-dimensional representation B_k; environment change times unknown
Learner knows N, d, r, task boundaries; tuning of CD-RepL uses S, theta_min, theta_max, nu, ell, kappa (minimum principal-angle sine between consecutive representations)
Task diversity assumption with parameters ell, nu; theta_min <= ||theta_s|| <= theta_max
settings.definition_quote: We further assume that these tasks are drawn from $m$ different environments ... for each environment $\CE_k$, there exists a matrix $B_k\in \R^{d\times r_k}$ with orthonormal columns such that $\theta_i=B_k \alpha_i$ ... The agent knows $\sigma(t),N,d$, and $r$, but has no knowledge of $\theta_i$, $B_k$, and $\tau_k$

settings.name_in_paper: Single linear bandit task (ellipsoid action set)
settings.definition_quote: Given a bandit task $\theta\in \mathcal T$, let the agent play it using RepE in Algorithm~\ref{alg:RE} for $N$ rounds.

bound.expression_latex: \tilde O \Big({d r \sqrt{\tau N}}+ {\frac{d r}{\lambda_0^2 \nu^2} \sqrt{\tau N}}+ \frac{d \ell}{r} \sqrt{\tau N } + \tau r \sqrt{N} \Big)

symbols.tau: number of tasks in the sequence (unknown to learner)
symbols.N_task: number of rounds per task (paper's N)
symbols.lambda_0: scale of exploration actions in A

conditions: Assumption 1: ellipsoid action set, theta_min <= ||theta|| <= theta_max

source.label: regret:seq:single_B
source.quote: Let the agent play the series of bandits in Eq.~\eqref{Sequ_tasks} using SeqRepL in Algorithm~\ref{alg:SeqRepL}. Select an $L$ such that $L =\Theta(\ell)$, and let $N_1=dr\sqrt{{N}/{L}}$ and $N_2=r\sqrt{N}$. Then, the regret $R_{\tau N}$ of SepRepL satisfies \BE [R_{\tau N}]= \tilde O (...)

results.notes: Total horizon is tau*N. Algorithm does not need tau. Proof ends with 'follows from L=Theta(r^2)', inconsistent with statement; recorded as stated.

bound.expression_latex: \tilde O\left( d r \sqrt{\tau N}+ {\frac{d r}{\lambda_0^2 \nu^2} \sqrt{\tau N}}+ \tau r \sqrt{N} \right)

source.label: Coro_seq
source.quote: Assume that $\ell$ in Assumption~\ref{Assump:diversity} is of the order of $r$, i.e., $\ell=\Theta(r^2)$. Let $N_1=d\sqrt{r N}$ and $N_2=r\sqrt{N}$. Then, the regret of SepRepL ... satisfies $\BE [R_{\tau N}]= \tilde O\left( d r \sqrt{\tau N}+ {\frac{d r}{\lambda_0^2 \nu^2} \sqrt{\tau N}}+ \tau r \sqrt{N} \right)$.

results.notes: Statement says 'order of r' but writes ell=Theta(r^2).

source.label: regret:RepL
source.quote: Given a bandit task $\theta\in \mathcal T$, let the agent play it using RepE in Algorithm~\ref{alg:RE} for $N$ rounds. Then, the regret $R_N$ of RepE satisfies $\BE [R_N] = O(N_1+\frac{N}{N_1}d^2)$.

results.notes: Paper's N (rounds per task) mapped to T.

conditions: theta = B alpha with B in R^{d x r} orthonormal
an estimate B_hat with ||B_hat^T B_perp||_F <= varepsilon is given

source.label: transfer:single
source.quote: Given a bandit task $\theta\in \mathcal T$, assume that there exists $B\in \R^{d\times r}$ with orthonormal columns such that $\theta = B \alpha$ ... Assume that an estimate $\hat B$ is known and satisfies $\|\hat B^\top B_\perp\|_F \le \varepsilon$. ... then the regret satisfies $\BE [R_N]= O( N_2+ \frac{N }{N_2}r^2+ N \varepsilon^2 ). $

results.notes: Requires side information B_hat; paper's N mapped to T.

bound.expression_latex: \tilde{O} \Big( \sum_{i=1}^{m} \big( {d r \sqrt{\tau_i N}}+ { \frac{d r}{\lambda_0^2 \nu^2} \sqrt{\tau_i N}} +\frac{d \ell}{r} \sqrt{\tau_iN } \big) + S r \sqrt{N} + S n_{\rm det}+ m b dr\sqrt{N\ell} + 2m \Big)

symbols.tau_i: number of tasks in environment segment i
symbols.n_det: number of probing actions per task, ceil(9(d-r)log(2S^2N)/(theta_min^2 lambda_0^2 kappa^2))
symbols.b_init: number of initial exploration cycles b (Eq. value:b)

source.label: upp-bound:CD-RepL
source.quote: Let the agent play the sequential bandits in $\CS$ using the CD-RepL in Algorithm~\ref{alg:main}. Let $L=\Theta(\ell)$, $n_{\rm det}$ and $\xi_{\rm det}$ be as in Eq.~\eqref{det_selection:m}, and $b$ be as in Eq.~\eqref{value:b}. Then, the regret of the CD-RepL satisfies \BE[R_{T}] = \tilde{O} (...)

results.notes: T = S N. Horizon marked known since tuning uses S.

source.quote: Assume that $\ell=\Theta(r)$, $1/(\lambda_0^2 \nu^2)=\Theta(1)$, and $\kappa$ satisfies \kappa \ge \max \big\{\min\{ p_1,p_2 \},\min \{p_3,p_4 \} \big\} ... Then, the regret of CD-RepL ... satisfies \BE [R_{SN}] = \tilde O \Big(\sum _{i=1}^{m} {d r \sqrt{ \tau_i N}}+ S r \sqrt{N} \Big).

results.notes: Text notes this is at most O~(d r sqrt(m S N) + S r sqrt(N)).
